results.title: Cheapest way to host a Node.js app in 2026 (real prices) - DEV Community
results.content:
Render and Heroku database prices come from the cheapest database for a small app comparison, which also covers Neon, Supabase and Turso free tiers. If you'd rather keep the database on SQLite, put the file on a persistent volume: a 1 GB Standard volume on Hubfly space costs about $0.01 a month. Never keep SQLite on a container's normal disk, because that disk is wiped on every redeploy.

### How the Hubfly space numbers add up [...] | Railway | 30-day trial with $5 credit, then $1 a month | Hobby $5 minimum, which includes $5 of usage | Usage at $10 per GB of RAM and $20 per vCPU a month |
| Fly.io | $1 free to start, then pay as you go | $2.19: shared-cpu-1x, 256 MB; 512 MB about $3.69 | Extra RAM $6 per GB a month; North America prices |
| Heroku | None | Basic $7: 0.5 GB | Eco $5 sleeps after 30 min of inactivity |

results.title: 2026: The State of Enterprise AI | Menlo Ventures
results.content: Established systems are being rebuilt for machine speed and scale. Databases are still the systems agents touch most (91% of AI apps), but they’re shifting from manually provisioned, long-lived systems behind applications that persist for years to high-volume, ephemeral ones that agents spin up, use, and discard for each task. The rise of providers like Neon\/Lakebase, Supabase, ClickHouse, and Archil shows this most strongly.
